subject.title: Synchronous crypto.createHash blocks Node.js event loop on large MCP schemas

question: Should this issue be treated as enough source proof to queue a bundled-MCP config-hash performance fix, or should maintainers ask for a focused reproduction that distinguishes large launch config from large returned tool schemas?
rationale: Source proves synchronous config hashing exists, but the reported schema example points at a different runtime surface and the correct fix boundary depends on which payload actually blocks Gateway heartbeats.

options.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
options.body: Request a small benchmark or live repro that shows whether large mcp.servers launch config or returned tool schemas block the Gateway path before queueing automation.

options.title: Queue Config-Hash Repair
options.body: Treat the synchronous mergedConfig hash path as sufficient proof and ask for a narrow nonblocking fingerprint helper with focused regression coverage.

options.title: Split Schema Catalog Follow-Up
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to config hashing and open or link a separate schema-catalog performance item if returned schemas are reproduced as the real source.

recommendation.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
recommendation.body: Request a small benchmark or live repro that shows whether large mcp.servers launch config or returned tool schemas block the Gateway path before queueing automation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent bundle-MCP and Gateway-adjacent work puts vincentkoc closest to the current config-hash/runtime boundary.
